body: I don't see why shared UVs could be a problem. I spent some time yesterday looking at what was wrong with that example and I concluded that I should do it from scratch (minecraft_ao was pretty hard to fix already :D)

Oh wait.

> `webgl_materials_video.html` is broken in r.60 because the two `Face3`s of each `CubeGeometry` face share some UVs.

I've re-read that. Yes, that's a problem.

> If sharing UVs is not OK, then all geometries will have to be checked for this bug.

It's everywhere, not just `CubeGeometry` -- all the places where geometries were `Face3`-ified.
I suspect I missed some. I'll double check as soon as I get some quiet time again. Good thing you spotted this!
Is sharing `UV`s a problem due to do with WebGLRenderer buffers?

I think @mrdoob may have misunderstood my statement. Maybe I should have made myself more clear.

`webgl_materials_video.html` was broken in r.60 because the two `Face3s` of each `CubeGeometry` face shared some UVs -- _and when the demo code changed the UVs of one face, it consequently also changed the UVs of another face_.

I do not see anything, in principle, incorrect in sharing UVs, but for consistency, I feel more comfortable not doing so.

> Is sharing `UV`s a problem due to do with WebGLRenderer buffers?

If you want to share UVs you're free to do so. But by default UVs shouldn't be shared. It just creates problems like the video example.

issue.title: Prevents faces being duplicated
issue.body:
Fixes #3897

There may still be related bugs where the same `THREE.Vector3` objects are reused in normals.

issue.title: Preserve face ordering in OBJLoader and OBJMTLLoader.
issue.body:
OBJ loaders did not correctly preserve vertex and face list ordering and were creating duplicate vertex entries, rather than letting faces share vertices. Reordering the faces was breaking our morph creation system, which relies on the mesh topology being fixed.

This should be as efficient as the code it replaces for large models (possibly very slightly more so, as it doesn't duplicate vertices, so should use a bit less memory). But it would be worth testing it against the large models referenced in #3937 and #3965, just to make sure.

issue.title: PlaneGeometry lost separate positions/UVs for each tile since r69
issue.body:
(Related to #5657)

There was a behavior change for PlaneGeometry (and possibly other geometry classes) in r69 not mentioned in the release notes so I believe it might have been overlooked and/or unwanted.

PlaneGeometry used to create separate a separate set of UVs for each face in r68 and earlier versions, as evidenced here: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/commit/fce86cbbdad7e774744cf4482a6fcc415ff9faa0#diff-53d98cf69b8d7487c6245714cec71128L74

UVs are now shared just like vertex positions, which makes creating tile maps with PlaneGeometry impossible. More importantly, it breaks existing code when upgrading to r69.

Was the change meant to happen or is it a bug? Is there some other class that provides the old behavior or should we build our own?
